changed_in.5.2: Adds `"isrunning"`, which answers whether the collector is running rather than stopped, and `"generational"` and `"incremental"`, which move the collector between an experimental generational mode and the incremental one a fresh state starts in. `"count"` answers with a second value beside the kilobyte figure: the same total in bytes, modulo 1024. A collection also runs finalizers for tables from here — before, only a full userdata could carry a `__gc` metamethod, and Lua code cannot create one.
changed_in.5.3: Drops `"generational"` and `"incremental"`; the collector is incremental and no option changes that. `"count"` answers with one value again, the second being recoverable from the fractional part of the first. `"step"` gains a defined meaning for `arg`, whose effect was left unspecified before: zero asks for one basic step, and any other value asks the collector to work as though that many kilobytes had just been allocated. A numeric `arg` also has to hold an exact whole-number value, where earlier versions truncate one carrying a fraction towards zero.
changed_in.5.4: Brings `"generational"` and `"incremental"` back as mode switches that carry the mode's tuning numbers — a minor and a major multiplier for the first; a pause, a step multiplier and a step size for the second — and both answer with the mode in force before the call. `"setpause"` and `"setstepmul"` still work and are deprecated in favour of `"incremental"`. `arg` is read only by the options that use it, so a value of the wrong type beside an option that ignores it is no longer refused.
changed_in.5.5: Drops `"setpause"` and `"setstepmul"`, and `"incremental"` and `"generational"` stop carrying tuning numbers: every collector parameter is read and set through the new `"param"` option, which names it as a string and answers with its previous value. `"param"` also reaches parameters the older options had no name for. `"step"` reads `arg` as a number of bytes rather than of kilobytes.
